text:
IncBot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High 5xx error rate detected for /v1/chat endpoints in prod (10m window). 5xx ~12%, median latency up from 220ms -> 580ms. Multiple customers reporting timeouts. Auto-escalating to #incidents.

Jamie (oncall): I'm on. Pulling gateway and runtime logs now. Any spike correlation with model rollouts or infra?

Ravi: Checking gateway. There is a clear surge of long-lived streaming connections to /v1/chat/stream from a handful of IPs. Also seeing increased tail latencies on g-pool-3. No model rollout flagged in deploys.

Megan: Embeddings and rerank traffic look steady. Rerank shows a small increase but 5xxs are concentrated on chat.

Jamie (oncall): Plan A (immediate mitigation): 1) Apply stricter per-key QPS to chat routes (reduce default chat qps from 20 -> 5). 2) Enable route-specific hard throttle for /v1/chat/stream to protect sockets. 3) Disable rerank autotriggering that fans out to chat for now. 4) Keep embeddings quotas unchanged. Any objections?

Ravi: No objections. That should cut down churn. I'll scope precise rate-limit payloads.

Megan: +1. Also suggest bumping background embeddings quota for internal pipelines that are hitting non-chat lanes so they don't get paused during reshaping. We can shift low-priority work away from chat.

Jamie (oncall): Good point. We'll adjust embeddings via weight-based shaping rather than raising customer quota.

Ravi: Executing rate-limit change now. Command: 
```
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/v1/ratelimits/apply \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"scope":"global","rules":[{"route":"/v1/chat","limit":5,"burst":10,"unit":"qps"},{"route":"/v1/chat/stream","limit":2,"burst":4,"unit":"qps"}]}'
```
I'll post response when applied.

OpsBot: Rate limit policy applied: chat -> 5 qps/burst 10, chat/stream -> 2 qps/burst 4. Policy id rl-20260309-17.

Jamie (oncall): Seeing immediate drop in error rate on gateway layer, backend tail latency still high for in-flight requests. Keep rate-limits for 10 min and observe.

Evan: Noting customer impact: high-volume chat customers (free-tier bots) will likely see request rejections. We should update status page and notify top 10 customers. Priya, can you draft a short status line?

Priya (support): On it. Suggested status: "Degraded: Chat generation experiencing elevated errors and latency. We have applied temporary rate limits to protect overall system. Some chat requests may be rejected or delayed. Engineers are investigating. Updates every 15 minutes." Want me to publish now?

Jamie (oncall): Publish now. Add note: engineering is throttling chat to preserve availability.

Priya (support): Status updated on page and customers notified via email for high-traffic accounts.

Ravi: Post-change metrics: 5xx down from 12% -> 3.1% in 2m, median latency back near 260ms. Good. But one service node g-pool-3 still shows elevated CPU and slow <kv-cache> evictions. Investigating.

Megan: Rerank autotrigger disabled (patch id: deploy-rl-110). That removes bulk fanout that was touching chat endpoints.

Jamie (oncall): Next mitigation if backend remains noisy: shift non-interactive chat requests into a lower-priority queue with a retry/backoff, and apply per-route quotas per-customer (reduce default for anonymous keys). Can infra apply per-customer limit policy for the top offenders?

Ravi: I can add temporary per-api-key caps for the 3 top offenders. Command: 
```
POST /internal/quotas/set {"api_key":"key-abc","route":"/v1/chat","qps":1}
POST /internal/quotas/set {"api_key":"key-def","route":"/v1/chat","qps":1}
POST /internal/quotas/set {"api_key":"key-xyz","route":"/v1/chat","qps":2}
```
Applying now.

OpsBot: Per-key caps applied for keys key-abc, key-def, key-xyz.

Evan: Monitoring customer impact dashboard. Two auto-scaled customers hit quota and got 429s; we've contacted their account owners. Overall user-visible errors dropping.

Jamie (oncall): Good. Keep rate-limits for 20 more minutes, then we'll gradually relax if stable. Tracker: incident-2026-03-09-chat-throttle.

Priya (support): Support notes: please add exact error text to KB: "Requests may be throttled with HTTP 429 during system protection policies." I'll triage open tickets accordingly.

Ravi: g-pool-3 CPU issue root cause: long-running KV cache compaction tasks coincident with a small leak in the streaming worker that holds file descriptors. Restarting worker on node g-pool-3 now.

DeployBot: Rolling restart job started on g-pool-3 (job id restart-2201). Expected ~90s disruption per worker; autoscaler will compensate.

Megan: After restart, tail latencies normalized on that node. Error rate steady at ~1.8%. Nice work.

Jamie (oncall): Summarize live mitigations performed: - Global chat QPS reduced to 5/burst10 - Streaming chat QPS to 2/burst4 - Disabled rerank autotrigger - Applied per-key caps for 3 high-volume keys - Restarted noisy worker node - Status page + customer notifications posted

Evan: Handoff note: Jamie, I can take the on-call for next 2 hours to monitor rollback and follow-up.

Jamie (oncall): Thanks, leaning out. Handoff to Evan at 03:30 UTC. Please keep the rate limits until we validate 30m of stable metrics.

Evan: Acknowledged. Follow-ups to open as action items: 1) implement automatic dynamic per-route shaping for chat vs embeddings (Ravi + Runtime) 2) add alert for abnormal streamer FD/leak (Megan) 3) refine per-customer default quotas and make per-route caps adjustable from console (Product/DevEx).

Priya (support): I'll update support playbook with the temporary mitigation steps and the 429 messaging.

Jamie (oncall): Closing active page for me. Evan, ping if anything spikes. :thumbsup:

Evan: Will do. Leaving thread open for post-incident notes and root-cause follow-up. Thanks team. :slightly_smiling_face:
